Definition: a consecrated thing or place, especially, a palace, sanctuary (whether of Jehovah or of idols) or asylum
BiblicalUsage: The sanctuary is the holy place where God dwells among His people, and the word runs from the tabernacle to the temple and beyond. God said, let them make Me a sanctuary that I may dwell among them, and He planted His people on the mountain of His inheritance; and when they were carried into exile, He promised to be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they went.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the sanctuary was always a promise, not a building. God dwells with His people, and when the building is gone, He Himself is the sanctuary, until the day the dwelling of God is with men.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
